problem: The CMS admin runtime failed because the single-element selector helper was overwritten by the collection selector helper, and a data-area collection binding also used the single-element helper.
root_cause: Selector helper responsibilities were not separated: querySelector and querySelectorAll shared one variable name and collection consumers were not contract-checked.
decision: Maintain distinct selector helpers and enforce that collection bindings use the querySelectorAll helper. The public /cms page-check remains the runtime acceptance layer.
prevention: Single-element CMS bindings use the querySelector helper.
Collection CMS bindings use the querySelectorAll helper.
Historical replay proves the two helpers resolve to different identifiers and the data-area binding uses the collection helper.
The /cms runtime page-check must remain free of JavaScript exceptions.
